A.notes: Solid senior-level subject line under 72 chars. Body drifts into prose ('are no longer needed now that... Also removes...') rather than terse bullets, making it the most verbose of the three. Captures the full change accurately.

B.notes: Tight subject + compact two-line body listing the three changes. Offers a one-liner alternative, showing awareness of preference for brevity. Clean, code-first, no filler.

C.notes: Shortest subject (~54 chars), terse body covering the three changes without restating the diff. Helpful note about appending a tracking ticket. Conventional, direct, no flowery language.

analysis: All three produce concise, senior-appropriate commit messages with subject lines under 72 characters that capture the essence (removing deprecated REST internals post-gRPC migration). C and B are nearly identical in quality: both lead with a clean what-and-why subject and a terse body enumerating the three changes (handlers, OpenAPI specs, CI stub generation). C edges ahead with the most compact subject and a practical aside about referencing a tracking ticket; B matches it closely and adds a useful one-liner variant. A is still strong but its body reads as connected prose rather than terse enumeration, making it marginally more verbose and slightly less aligned with a concise, code-first style. None include 'Great question!' filler or multi-paragraph over-explanation, so differences are fine-grained matters of terseness.
